title: T-65B X-wing (Star Wars: Squadrons)

sources.title: STAR WARS: Squadrons PC text manual (EA accessibility resources)

intro: The X-wing in Star Wars: Squadrons is the New Republic's balanced fighter with shields. It is good at most jobs, neither the fastest nor the toughest. Its wings split open into an X for attack.

panels.name: T-65B X-wing: class and loadout
panels.text: This lists the X-wing's class and its parts as the hangar shows them.
panels.context: All other controls work as in every Squadrons ship; the parts (components) can be changed in the hangar before a battle.

controls.name: Pilot seat
controls.text: The X-wing has a single-seat cockpit: one pilot and no crew.
controls.context: The pilot flies alone and does every job: flying, shooting, power and team messages.

controls.name: Class: fighter
controls.text: The X-wing is a fighter of the New Republic, an all-round ship.
controls.context: The class decides the ship's role in a battle and which components the hangar offers for it.

controls.name: Laser cannons (four)
controls.text: Four laser cannons at the wingtips fire as the primary weapon.
controls.context: They fire with the trigger; more weapon power on the hat lets them fire longer.

controls.name: S-foils
controls.text: The X-wing's wings (S-foils) open into the X shape in attack position.
controls.context: The split wings are the X-wing's trademark; open wings show the ship is ready to fight.

controls.name: Auxiliaries (left and right)
controls.text: The X-wing carries two auxiliary components: the left one on button 3, the right one on button 4.
controls.context: Head buttons 3 and 4 on the stick use them; the auxiliary status display shows their cooldown.

controls.name: Countermeasures
controls.text: The X-wing's countermeasure component sits on head button 6 of the stick.
controls.context: Head button 6 fires it; it is the answer to a missile warning.

controls.name: Button 7: shield focus
controls.text: On this New Republic ship base button 7 is shield focus: it points the shields to the front or the back.
controls.context: Pointing the shields at the enemy protects the side that is being hit.
